nominal_positions.interpretation: Extent under dhāvasi. Sāyaṇa supplies masculine deśa. Neuter measure and masculine accusative coincide here.
Second extent, a longer journey under Sāyaṇa’s interpretation. The coalesced final consonant before the next vowel leaves its case unchanged.
Short-i extent of running. Masculine agreement with the commentary’s supplied place and a nominal measure are compatible with the same ending.
Long-ī compound measuring the location. Masculine deśa supplied in the printed exposition.
Short-i attribute of the seven metres recited for the divine twins.
The Aśvin recitation is the ritual setting in which other deities have a share.

source_policy_decisions.decision: The three distance expressions belong to the act of running. The requested return is a later clause. Use one case credit for a syncretic expression with an understood place.

The underived comparison unit of 5.2.19 cannot supply the short i. The horseman analysis gives an explicit segmental account. Preserve the independently observed accent and its open historical explanation.
Aitareya supplies a single compound in the locative. One thousand recitations and a thousand horse-days occupy different positions in the argument.
The short-i deity relation is independently fixed by the recited metres and by the named contest. It receives no metric reading.
The measured thousand in Aitareya, the three alternatives under dhāvasi and PG776’s previously located Pañcaviṃśa parallels leave the exact hundred-flight quotation Open.
